    • handleBind

      protected void handleBind(ServerSocketChannel ssc, SocketAddress sa) throws IOException
      Bind the given address to the given ServerSocketChannel. By default, this just calls `ssc.bind(sa)`, but you may handle some exceptions by overriding this method in a subclass.
      Parameters:
      ssc - The server socket channel.
      sa - The socket address to bind to.
      Throws:
      IOException - on error.

    • handleConnect

      protected boolean handleConnect(SocketChannel sc, SocketAddress sa) throws IOException
      Connect the given SocketChannel with the given address. By default, this just calls `sc.connect(sa)`, but you may handle some exceptions by overriding this method in a subclass.
      Parameters:
      sc - The socket channel.
      sa - The socket address to connect to.
      Throws:
      IOException - on error.

    • resolveAddressForSecondBind

      protected SocketAddress resolveAddressForSecondBind(SocketAddress originalAddress, ServerSocketChannel ssc) throws IOException
      Returns the temporary address usable to binding on for a second bind. Depending on the socket domain, a wildcard address may be permittable or not for a second bind.
      Parameters:
      originalAddress - The original temporary address (e.g., a wildcard address).
      ssc - The socket that was bound to that address.
      Returns:
      The local bound address, or the originalAddress.
      Throws:
      IOException - on error.
      See Also:
      • testDoubleBindAddressReusable()

    • socketDomainPermitsDoubleBind

      protected boolean socketDomainPermitsDoubleBind()
      Override to declare that a certain socket domain permits double-binding an address, particularly when the address is comparable to a wildcard address.

      true iff double-binding the same address is allowed.
